title: Zoom in: one booking transaction, from BEGIN to a durable commit
caption: Locks are held only inside the transaction; the commit waits for exactly one thing, the standby's WAL flush.

messages.label: BEGIN
messages.note: Transaction mode: the pooler lends one server connection for this transaction only.

messages.label: SELECT … room_nights FOR UPDATE
messages.note: Locks just the two room-night rows; other rooms stay free to book.

messages.label: INSERT booking; UPDATE avail - 1
messages.note: A CHECK (avail >= 0) constraint is the last line of defence against overbooking.

messages.label: COMMIT
messages.note: The primary writes the commit record to its WAL.

messages.label: WAL up to commit record
messages.note: Streaming replication; the commit is not confirmed yet.

messages.label: flushed
messages.note: ~1 ms in the same region. This is the price of zero data loss.

messages.label: COMMIT ok
messages.note: Row locks are released now.

messages.label: booking b_91
messages.note: The server connection goes back to the pool for the next transaction.

messages.label: same WAL (async)
messages.note: The replica applies it a few ms later; nobody waits for it.

scenarios.name: Sync standby down
scenarios.summary: With one sync standby and no fallback, commits wait forever when it disappears; a quorum of two standbys (ANY 1) keeps commits flowing.

messages.label: BEGIN … COMMIT
messages.note: Same transaction as before.

messages.label: COMMIT
messages.note: The commit record is written locally.

messages.label: WAL up to commit record
messages.note: The standby host has just died.

messages.label: wait for standby ack
messages.note: Locks stay held, and every booking for these rooms queues behind them.

messages.label: timeout after 5 s
messages.note: The client sees an error even though the commit may still complete. Retries need an idempotency key.

messages.label: (ANY 1 of 2) second standby acks
messages.note: Fix: synchronous_standby_names = 'ANY 1 (sb1, sb2)'. One standby can die without stopping writes.

scenarios.name: Lock wait timeout
scenarios.summary: A batch job holds the rows a guest wants; lock_timeout fails the booking fast instead of letting it hang.

messages.label: batch: UPDATE room_nights (10 000 rows)
messages.note: A nightly repricing job locks many rows in one long transaction.

messages.label: BEGIN
messages.note: A guest books one of those rooms.

messages.label: SELECT … FOR UPDATE
messages.note: Has to wait for the batch to commit.

messages.label: lock_timeout (2 s) exceeded
messages.note: Bounded wait: the guest's request fails fast instead of holding a connection for a minute.

messages.label: 409, try again
messages.note: The API retries once with backoff, or shows 'just a moment'.

messages.label: batch: commit every 500 rows
messages.note: Fix the cause: short transactions keep lock windows small.

scenarios.name: Alternative: async commit
scenarios.summary: Skip the standby wait: commits are ~1 ms faster, but a crash can lose the last confirmed bookings.

messages.label: BEGIN … COMMIT
messages.note: Same transaction.

messages.label: COMMIT
messages.note: synchronous_commit = local: confirm after the local WAL flush only.

messages.label: COMMIT ok
messages.note: No network round-trip in the commit path.

messages.label: WAL (async)
messages.note: Sent right after, usually within ms.

messages.label: last 200 ms of WAL
messages.note: The primary's host fails before sending it: those bookings are gone after failover, although guests were told they succeeded.
